findings.title: `viscosity > 0` forecloses the inviscid / truncated-Euler limit, which the solver handles exactly
findings.after:
viscosity > 0 ||
    throw(ArgumentError("`viscosity` must be positive, got $viscosity: it sets the Reynolds number " *
                        "through Re = 1/ν, and a non-positive value has no dissipation scale"))
findings.why_it_matters: ν = 0 was previously valid and numerically well-formed everywhere it is consumed: `velocity_integrating_factor` returns `coefficient = -generator.conditions.viscosity * τ` = 0, so `exponential_convolve!` applies the identity, and `dissipation` multiplies by ν to give exactly 0. Nothing NaNs. A Galerkin-truncated Euler run (Cichowlas-style thermalization, an inviscid cascade study, a pure-advection passive-scalar test at κ = ν/Sc = 0) is a standard DNS workflow this package could previously run and now cannot — `Simulation(domain; viscosity = 0.0)` throws at construction. The check also sits on the shared public `FlowConditions` constructor, not only the `Simulation` front door, so it removes the regime from every entry point at once.
findings.disposition: PLAUSIBLE — the inviscid limit is a real study and this guard forecloses it. I added it to close a NaN-scalar route that `schmidt` validation already closes. OPEN, for the user.

findings.title: `allocate_buffers(AdamsBashforth, tracers)` deleted: multistep tracers now require an `ObservablesCache` and two resident N³ fields
findings.after:
function allocate_buffers(::AdamsBashforth{K}, tracers::Tracers, cache) where {K}
  length(cache.particle_velocity_history) >= K - 1 ||
    throw(ArgumentError("this cache carries $(length(cache.particle_velocity_history)) past " *
                        "sample(s), but `AdamsBashforth(order = $K)` integrates over $(K - 1); " *
                        "build the cache with `history_depth = $K`"))
findings.why_it_matters: The two-argument form is still the *only* one documented — `Propagator.jl:148` reads ``allocate_buffers(scheme, tracers) -> ParticleIntegratorBuffers`` and `ParticleIntegratorBuffers`'s own docstring repeats it — yet for `AdamsBashforth` it now MethodErrors. The `Tracers` docstring advertises exactly this workflow ("advance them by hand … the scheme's per-step storage is yours to allocate"); a hand-run tracer loop over an externally supplied velocity field, with no `ObservablesCache` in the picture, is now impossible at order > 1. To get it back the caller must build an `ObservablesCache(domain; history_depth = K)`, whose constructor unconditionally allocates `new_vector_field_physical(domain)` twice — two full N³ vector fields — purely to house (K−1) M×3 sample arrays. That inverts invariant 4 ("minimal memory footprint trumps compute cost"). The type's documented fields `past` / `steps` / `filled` were removed at the same time, breaking any reader of them.

findings.title: `cfl_timestep` gained a unit-dependent ceiling that silently shortens Δt for any run with max speed below 1
findings.before: return speed > 0 ? sim.cfl * Δx / speed : sim.cfl * Δx
findings.after:
ceiling = sim.cfl * Δx
  return speed > 0 ? min(sim.cfl * Δx / speed, ceiling) : ceiling
findings.why_it_matters: This is not a rejection but a silent change of computed result on previously valid input. Whenever `max_speed < 1` in code units, the adaptive step is now clamped to `cfl·Δx` instead of `cfl·Δx/speed` — a different Δt sequence, hence a different trajectory, for a run that was correct before. The threshold is `speed == 1`, which carries no physics: `cfl·Δx` is a *length*, and calling it "the step at unit speed" makes the cap depend entirely on the caller's choice of velocity units. A run in dimensional units (side_length = 0.1 m, u ~ 0.01 m/s) or simply a low-energy run (`kinetic_energy = 0.1` gives u' ≈ 0.26) is throttled by orders of magnitude with no message. The underlying defect — an unforced run decaying toward u_max → 0 and Δt running away — is real, but a runaway guard belongs at a physically motivated scale (a fraction of a turnover time, a `max_dt` setting the caller can see), not at whatever step the same formula yields when the speed happens to equal one.
findings.disposition: CONFIRMED BY HAND — measured 1.9x cut (max_speed 0.525: 0.374 -> 0.196). The ceiling binds at u_max < 1, a bare number against a dimensional velocity, so it is unit-dependent. OPEN, for the user.

findings.title: `randn!` into device storage breaks `StochasticOU` on GPU, the package's primary target
findings.before: copyto!(field_data(noise_physical), randn(ou.rng, T, size(field_data(noise_physical))...))
findings.after: randn!(ou.rng, field_data(noise_physical))
findings.why_it_matters: `ou.rng` is a `MersenneTwister` (set in the constructor) and `field_data(noise_physical)` is the domain's array type — a `CuArray`/`ROCArray` on a device backend, since the scratch comes from `new_vector_field_physical(domain)`. `Random.randn!(::MersenneTwister, ::AbstractArray)` falls back to a scalar `A[i] = randn(rng, T)` loop, which a device array refuses (scalar indexing disallowed) or executes catastrophically slowly. The old line was deliberately host-side-then-copy, and the docstring still documents that contract verbatim: "!!! note \"The random increment is generated host-side\" … on the GPU this is a portability-first choice, not yet a performance-tuned one." A GPU run with `StochasticOU` forcing worked before and does not now. The allocation the edit set out to remove is real, but the proportionate fix keeps a persistent host buffer and copies, rather than handing a host RNG a device array.
findings.disposition: DISPUTED, NOT DISMISSED — flagged independently by three lanes. An earlier round-5 witness ran on the RTX 5070 Ti under allowscalar(false) and passed, citing GPUArrays' own randn! method. Corroboration outweighs my single counter-witness; needs a real GPU check before anyone acts. OPEN.

findings.title: `_base_cfl(::AbstractIntegrator)` fallback removed, contradicting the documented "may specialize" contract for user schemes
findings.before: _base_cfl(::AbstractIntegrator) = 0.3
findings.after:
# NO `::AbstractIntegrator` FALLBACK, matching `allocate_buffers` on the same supertype: a scheme
# that has not declared its stability limit gets a hard error, not a number.
findings.why_it_matters: The `AbstractIntegrator` docstring says a scheme "implements `step!` … and **may** specialize `recommended_cfl`" — optional by construction. `Simulation`'s `cfl` keyword defaults to `recommended_cfl(scheme, domain)`, so a user-defined scheme that took the documented option of *not* specializing now MethodErrors at run construction, where it previously received 0.3. The removed fallback is the only thing that made the documented optionality real, and the replacement hook `_base_cfl` is unexported internal — the user's only legitimate route is to specialize the public `recommended_cfl`, which no docstring tells them is now mandatory. The stated defect (0.3 sits above `IFRK2`'s 0.25, so a tighter new scheme would be over-stepped) argues for lowering the fallback, not deleting the extension point.

findings.title: `ModelSpectrum` lost its public `ref` field, and `provenance` now throws for combinations the module advertises
findings.before:
struct ModelSpectrum{L<:LargeScaleFactor, D<:DissipationFactor} <: EnergySpectrum
  C_K::Float64
  large_scale::L
  dissipation::D
  ref::Reference
end

provenance(m::ModelSpectrum) = m.ref
findings.after:
provenance(m::ModelSpectrum) = _reference(m.large_scale, m.dissipation)

_reference(::PopeLargeScale, ::PopeDissipation) = _POPE2000
_reference(::VonKarmanLarge, ::UnitDissipation) = _VONKARMAN1948
_reference(::UnitLargeScale, ::PaoDissipation) = _PAO1965
_reference(::LargeScaleFactor, ::DissipationFactor) =
  throw(ArgumentError("this combination of large-scale and dissipation factors is not a published " *
                      "model, so it has no reference; the named presets each carry one"))
findings.why_it_matters: The type's own docstring invites the very usage now rejected — "Build one directly to mix roll-off forms" — and the module map advertises `ExponentialDissipation` and `SaffmanDissipation` as swappable factors. Neither appears in the three-entry `_reference` table, so every model built from them now throws on `provenance`, a function `Phenomenology.jl` documents as part of what a law *is* ("A concrete law … reports its `provenance`"). Previously a user composing a mixed model supplied their own `Reference` through the documented four-argument positional constructor, which is now gone while the surviving prose still reads "`ref` is its `Reference`". The GPU motive is genuine (a `Reference` carries `String`s, and `SimulationRun.jl:330`'s `ic_spectrum = κ -> spectrum(initial_spectrum, κ, fp)` captures the model into a device kernel), but the proportionate fix strips the reference at the capture site or keeps `provenance` total by returning a default; deleting a public field and making a documented accessor partial is wider than the defect required.

findings.title: `kinetic_energy > 0` rejects a zero-energy seed, which the seeder previously realized correctly
findings.before:
function Simulation(domain::FixedDomain;
                    kinetic_energy::Real = 1.5, κ_max_η = nothing, viscosity = nothing,
findings.after:
kinetic_energy > 0 ||
    throw(ArgumentError("`kinetic_energy` must be positive, got $kinetic_energy: it is " *
                        "k = ½⟨|u|²⟩, which cannot be negative, and a zero-energy field has no " *
                        "spectrum to seed"))
findings.why_it_matters: The stated defect is a *negative* value reaching `sqrt`; the check is one strictness wider and takes zero with it. `kinetic_energy = 0` previously worked and produced exactly what a physicist would expect: `random_solenoidal_velocity_spectral!` measures a positive `current_energy`, rescales by `sqrt(0/current) = 0`, and hands back a quiescent field. That is the natural setup for a pure passive-scalar diffusion run, a tracer-interpolation test in still fluid, or a state the caller intends to overwrite incrementally with `fields_modified!`. The error message's justification is also false against the code it guards — the seeder does have a spectrum to seed and does seed it. Only the grid-mode branch genuinely needs k > 0 (ε = 0 would give ν = 0), and that branch is reached only when `viscosity` is not passed.

findings.title: The forcing's `1e-12` band floor was removed outright, inverting `ConstantPower` behaviour on weak fields
findings.before:
band_value < 1e-12 && return field                   # nothing in the band yet (guard)
…
  amplitude = band_observable > 1e-12 ? forcing.injection_rate / (2 * band_observable) : 0.0
findings.after:
_band_is_empty(band_value) && return field           # nothing in the band yet
…
  amplitude = _band_is_empty(band_observable) ? 0.0 :
              forcing.injection_rate / (2 * band_observable)
…
_band_is_empty(band_value) = !(isfinite(band_value) && band_value > zero(band_value))
findings.why_it_matters: The scale-invariance argument is sound and the direction is under-rejection rather than over-, but it silently changes a computed result for previously valid input in the destabilizing direction. A legitimately weak field — a scalar seeded at `scalar_variance = 1e-14`, or a Float32 run whose band observable sits just above the old floor — used to be left alone by `ConstantPower` (amplitude 0). It now receives `injection_rate / (2 · 1e-14)`, an amplitude of order 1e13 applied on the first step. The old floor was a crude absolute threshold and deserved to go, but replacing it with bare positivity removes any bound on the derived amplitude; nothing in the edit caps what the reciprocal can produce.

findings.title: ModelSpectrum loses its `ref` field and positional arity, and `provenance` now throws for any non-cataloged strategy combination
findings.before:
struct ModelSpectrum{L<:LargeScaleFactor, D<:DissipationFactor} <: EnergySpectrum
  C_K::Float64
  large_scale::L
  dissipation::D
  ref::Reference
end
...
provenance(m::ModelSpectrum) = m.ref
findings.after:
struct ModelSpectrum{L<:LargeScaleFactor, D<:DissipationFactor} <: EnergySpectrum
  C_K::Float64
  large_scale::L
  dissipation::D
end
...
provenance(m::ModelSpectrum) = _reference(m.large_scale, m.dissipation)
_reference(::PopeLargeScale, ::PopeDissipation) = _POPE2000
_reference(::VonKarmanLarge, ::UnitDissipation) = _VONKARMAN1948
_reference(::UnitLargeScale, ::PaoDissipation) = _PAO1965
_reference(::LargeScaleFactor, ::DissipationFactor) =
  throw(ArgumentError("this combination of large-scale and dissipation factors is not a published model, so it has no reference; the named presets each carry one"))
findings.why_it_matters: The real defect was narrow (a Reference-carrying struct is not a bitstype, blocking GPU capture of the seeding closure) and only required NOT storing the reference inline. The fix goes much further: it drops the 4th positional constructor argument outright (any call site using `ModelSpectrum(C_K, large_scale, dissipation, ref)` now gets a MethodError), and it replaces free user-supplied provenance with a closed 3-combination lookup that throws ArgumentError for every other large_scale/dissipation pairing. ModelSpectrum's own docstring documents 5 dissipation factors (Pope/Unit/Pao/Exponential/Saffman) and 3 large-scale factors (Pope/VonKarman/Unit) and says 'Build one directly to mix roll-off forms' — of the ~15 combinations this composable strategy-pattern type advertises, only 3 still produce a working `provenance`; every other legitimately constructible, previously-citable ModelSpectrum (e.g. PopeLargeScale + SaffmanDissipation with a user-supplied citation) now silently constructs fine but throws the first time anything calls `provenance` on it. Nothing in the current docstring (which still contains a dangling, non-antecedent line — '`ref` is its Reference' — left over from the old 4-arg form) tells a reader this landmine exists.

findings.title: allocate_buffers for AdamsBashforth silently gained a required 3rd argument; the public home docstring still documents the old 2-arg form
findings.why_it_matters: Any existing user code that built AdamsBashforth particle buffers with the documented, exported, 2-argument call `allocate_buffers(AdamsBashforth(order = 4), tracers)` now gets a MethodError, since the 2-arg method was deleted rather than kept as a deprecated/compatibility overload. Worse, src/Propagator.jl's home docstring for the exported `allocate_buffers` (unchanged by this round) still reads 'allocate_buffers(scheme, tracers) -> ParticleIntegratorBuffers ... The second serves the trajectory schemes ... One generic covers both' — it never mentions that the trajectory-scheme form now needs a 3rd `cache` argument for AdamsBashforth. A reader following the published contract to the letter writes code that no longer compiles, with no note anywhere that the arity changed.

findings.title: MultistepBuffers is a completely different struct — all four fields renamed/replaced, mutability dropped
findings.why_it_matters: MultistepBuffers is exported. Any code that read buffers.past, buffers.steps, or buffers.filled directly (the fields the pre-existing docstring described: '`past` — the previous Lagrangian samples... `steps`... `filled`') now fails to compile — those fields no longer exist. The struct also changed from mutable (with a mutable filled::Int) to plain immutable, and the positional field order/count is entirely different (4 fields, none matching the old 4 by name, type, or position). This is a wider rewrite than 'move the history into the cache' strictly required: the same relocation could have kept past/steps as thin forwarding properties or preserved field names for the parts that still exist (startup), rather than replacing the whole field set silently under the same type name.

findings.title: ObservablesCache gained a 4th type parameter and 3 new struct fields, and max_speed's type is no longer fixed to Float64
findings.before:
mutable struct ObservablesCache{PV, PS, TS}
  const velocity_physical::PV
  const vorticity_physical::PV
  const scalar_physical::PS
  const particle_velocities::TS
  velocity_epoch::Int
  vorticity_epoch::Int
  scalar_epoch::Int
  max_speed::Float64
  max_speed_epoch::Int
  sample_fields_epoch::Int
  sample_particles_epoch::Int
  fields_epoch::Int
  particles_epoch::Int
end
findings.after:
mutable struct ObservablesCache{PV, PS, TS, T <: AbstractFloat}
  const velocity_physical::PV
  const vorticity_physical::PV
  const scalar_physical::PS
  const particle_velocities::TS
  const particle_velocity_history::Vector{TS}
  const sample_steps::Vector{Float64}
  history_filled::Int
  velocity_epoch::Int
  vorticity_epoch::Int
  scalar_epoch::Int
  max_speed::T
  max_speed_epoch::Int
  ...
end
findings.why_it_matters: Any code that names the concrete type with 3 parameters (ObservablesCache{PV,PS,TS}, e.g. in a function signature or isa check written against the old struct) no longer matches the real type, which now has 4 parameters and a completely different field ordering (3 new fields inserted before the epoch counters). Separately, cache.max_speed (and deposit_max_speed!'s stored value) is no longer unconditionally Float64 — it is now T = real(eltype(field_data(velocity))), so a Float32 run now stores and returns a Float32. Existing code that collected cache.max_speed values into a Vector{Float64}, or otherwise assumed the accessor always returns Float64, now gets a type mismatch on Float32 runs. This part is at least announced in the docstring ('a host number in the field's own element type'), which the type-parameter arity change is not.

findings.title: cfl_timestep now caps the adaptive timestep, changing computed Δt for every run whose max speed drops below O(1) in code units — not only the pathological blow-up case
findings.before:
isfinite(speed) || error("non-finite velocity at step $(sim.clock.step): the run appears to have blown up")
  return speed > 0 ? sim.cfl * Δx / speed : sim.cfl * Δx
findings.after:
isfinite(speed) || error("non-finite velocity at step $(sim.clock.step): the run appears to have blown up")
  ceiling = sim.cfl * Δx
  return speed > 0 ? min(sim.cfl * Δx / speed, ceiling) : ceiling
findings.why_it_matters: This changes a computed result for every Simulation using the default adaptive dt path once max_speed(cache) < 1 (in the code's length/time units) — not merely the extreme decay-to-zero pathology the comment describes (Δt ≈ 1e15). Any run that legitimately has sub-unit velocity at some point (a decaying-turbulence tail, a weak scalar-only run, a deliberately slow flow) now takes a different, smaller Δt than before at that point, silently changing the exact trajectory and step count reproduced from a given seed/config versus a prior run of the same setup. The ceiling's scale (sim.cfl * Δx, i.e. implicitly assuming a characteristic speed of 1) is tied to this package's own convention (default kinetic_energy = 1.5 gives rms speed ≈ 1) rather than to any property of the Simulation object itself, so it is a global assumption baked into a public function with no keyword to adjust or disable it.

findings.title: step! now returns state instead of the (û, φ̂) tuple both concrete methods actually returned — a real behavior change, though it restores a pre-existing (already published) docstring contract
findings.before:
finalize!(generator, state, domain)             # post-step forcing projections (e.g. BandRescaling)
  fields_modified!(cache)                     # the step advanced the fields — the cache goes stale
  return û, φ̂
end
findings.after:
finalize!(generator, state, domain)             # post-step forcing projections (e.g. BandRescaling)
  advance_fields_epoch!(cache)                # the step advanced the fields — the cache goes stale
  return state
end
findings.why_it_matters: Applied identically to both step!(::IFLowStorageRK3, ...) and step!(::IFRK2, ...). Any hand-run loop written against the code's actual prior behavior — û, φ̂ = step!(scheme, state, generator, domain, buffers, dt) — now gets a ResolvedFields object where it destructured a 2-tuple, and breaks. The mitigating factor is that function step! end's home docstring already said 'Returns `state`.' before this round (verified against the pre-diff base commit), so this fixes a genuine docs/code mismatch rather than introducing a new undocumented one — but the change is still silent for any caller who had been relying on the tuple the code, not the docs, actually delivered.

findings.title: _base_cfl loses its AbstractIntegrator fallback, so a hand-written custom integrator that used to get a default recommended_cfl now gets a MethodError
findings.before:
_base_cfl(::AbstractIntegrator) = 0.3
_base_cfl(::IFRK2) = 0.25
_base_cfl(::IFLowStorageRK3) = 0.5
findings.after:
_base_cfl(::IFRK2) = 0.25
_base_cfl(::IFLowStorageRK3) = 0.5
findings.why_it_matters: recommended_cfl is exported and public; AbstractIntegrator is the documented extension point for adding a new time-stepping scheme. Previously any new AbstractIntegrator subtype without its own _base_cfl method silently got 0.3 from recommended_cfl; now it throws a MethodError from deep inside recommended_cfl (naming an internal, unexported helper the implementer never sees in the public docs) instead of a clear message pointing at the missing method. This is a smaller-impact case than the others because _base_cfl itself is unexported and not part of the documented six-verb generator protocol, so the practical audience affected is narrow.

findings.title: deposit! now throws for a scalar-carrying state paired with a scalar-less cache, where it previously silently skipped the scalar deposit
findings.before:
function deposit!(cache::ObservablesCache, state::ResolvedFields, domain::FixedDomain,
                  buffers::IntegratorBuffers)
  u = take_velocity!(cache)
  ...
findings.after:
function deposit!(cache::ObservablesCache, state::ResolvedFields, domain::FixedDomain,
                  buffers::IntegratorBuffers)
  state.scalar_spectral === nothing || cache.scalar_physical !== nothing ||
    throw(ArgumentError("this state carries a passive scalar but the cache has no scalar slot to receive it, so the scalar would be evolved and never observed. Build the cache with `scalar = true`."))
  u = take_velocity!(cache)
  ...
findings.why_it_matters: Any hand-assembled run that (intentionally or not) paired a scalar-carrying ResolvedFields with a scalar-less ObservablesCache — previously accepted, silently dropping the scalar deposit every iteration — now throws ArgumentError at the very first deposit! call. This is a defensible defensive check (it catches a real construction mistake with no other symptom), so the narrowing is well-targeted to the defect it fixes; flagged here only because it is, by the letter of the audit's own criterion, usage that used to run without error and no longer does.

findings.title: StochasticOU's in-place randn! breaks the GPU backend the fix claims to help
findings.before: copyto!(field_data(noise_physical), randn(ou.rng, T, size(field_data(noise_physical))...))
findings.after:
# In place: `randn` would allocate a fresh field-scale array on every step of the hot loop, and on
  # a device backend a host array to copy across as well.
  randn!(ou.rng, field_data(noise_physical))
findings.why_it_matters: `noise_physical` is `new_vector_field_physical(domain)`/`new_scalar_field_physical(domain)` — allocated "on the domain's backend" (SimulationDomain.jl), i.e. a CuArray/ROCArray on a GPU run, since GPU is stated as the package's primary target. `ou.rng` is a `MersenneTwister` (host-only RNG). Calling `randn!(rng::MersenneTwister, x::AbstractArray)` on a device array dispatches to Julia's generic fallback, which fills the array element-by-element via `setindex!` — exactly the "scalar indexing of device arrays" the invariants forbid, and something CUDA.jl/AMDGPU.jl either throws on (`allowscalar(false)`) or executes catastrophically slowly. The identical random-increment need is solved correctly two files away, unmodified by this diff: `src/State.jl` still does `copyto!(field_data(noise), randn(rng, T, physical_field_shape(...)...))` — generate on the host, then copy across to the device array — the GPU-safe idiom this same codebase already established for the same operation. The fix removed a real per-step host allocation, but did so by deleting the host-generate/device-copy pattern instead of only the allocation inside it (e.g. `randn!` into a preallocated host scratch array, then `copyto!`), leaving one correct and one broken implementation of the same primitive in the same package. It is wider than the defect (an allocation) required: it also silently drops GPU support for `StochasticOU`, contradicting invariant 4's GPU-primary/no-scalar-indexing guarantee.
findings.disposition: DISPUTED, NOT DISMISSED — flagged independently by three lanes. An earlier round-5 witness ran on the RTX 5070 Ti under allowscalar(false) and passed, citing GPUArrays' own randn! method. Corroboration outweighs my single counter-witness; needs a real GPU check before anyone acts. OPEN.

findings.title: New per-step scalar-variance reduction and host readback added to advance!, uncounted against the frozen sync/compute ledgers
findings.before: (no scalar blow-up check existed in advance!; only cfl_timestep checked isfinite(speed) on the velocity, and only on the adaptive-timestep path)
findings.after:
isfinite(max_speed(sim.cache)) ||
    error("non-finite velocity at step $(sim.clock.step + 1): the run appears to have blown up")
  # ... This costs one extra reduction and one readback, and only on a run that carries a scalar.
  sim.state.scalar_spectral === nothing ||
    isfinite(scalar_variance(sim.state.scalar_spectral)) ||
    error("non-finite scalar at step $(sim.clock.step + 1): the run appears to have blown up")
findings.why_it_matters: `scalar_variance(φ) = inner(φ, φ)` is a fresh whole-field spectral reduction with a device-to-host sync, and it is not deposited/cached anywhere else in the step — this call computes it from scratch every single `advance!` on any scalar-carrying run, forever, not just occasionally. The author's own comment concedes the cost ("this costs one extra reduction and one readback"). CLAUDE.md's memory note explicitly tracks host-device sync count per step as an audited quantity ("the 8th axis, default 3 readbacks/step vs floor 1") and the verification workflow requires that a step-schedule/cost change update the frozen ledgers in the same commit, citing the decision. This diff (scoped to src/) shows no such ledger update alongside a change that raises the per-step readback count for every scalar run. The underlying defect (an undetected scalar-only blow-up) is real, but the fix widens the routine per-step cost of every scalar simulation rather than being scoped and reconciled against the audit apparatus this repository built specifically to police exactly this kind of change.

findings.title: _wrap! doubles the per-step broadcast pass over particle positions for every trajectory step
findings.before:
Xstar .= mod.(X .+ Δt .* v1, L)
  ...
  X .= mod.(X .+ (Δt / 2) .* (v1 .+ v2), L)
findings.after:
function _wrap!(X, L)
  X .= mod.(X, L)
  X .= ifelse.(X .== L, zero(eltype(X)), X)
  return X
end
...
  Xstar .= X .+ Δt .* v1
  _wrap!(Xstar, L)
  ...
  X .= X .+ (Δt / 2) .* (v1 .+ v2)
  _wrap!(X, L)
findings.why_it_matters: Every particle-position update in both EndpointHeun (two stages) and AdamsBashforth now costs two full broadcast passes over the position array instead of one, unconditionally, to correct a boundary case (mod landing exactly on L) that only some steps ever trigger. The array is M×3 (particle count), not field-scale, so the absolute cost is small, but it is new work placed unconditionally into the routine per-step particle path for every tracer-carrying run regardless of whether the boundary case ever occurs.

findings.title: Round-4 commit calls a landed fix "Deferred" — the message misstates what its own diff does
findings.before: velocity_forcing = BandRescaling(domain; target = kinetic_energy, over = :total),
findings.after: velocity_forcing = d -> BandRescaling(d; target = kinetic_energy, over = :total),
findings.why_it_matters: Commit ea5729769399 ("Round 4") lists this exact defect under its own "FIXED (19)" heading — "The default `velocity_forcing` was built in a KEYWORD DEFAULT, evaluated before the body, so a bad `kinetic_energy` was reported as a bad forcing `target` the user never set." — and then appends the single word "Deferred." But the diff in that SAME commit changes the default from an eagerly-constructed `BandRescaling(domain; …)` (evaluated before the function body runs, i.e. before the `kinetic_energy > 0` guard the commit is simultaneously adding) to a lazily-materialized `d -> BandRescaling(d; …)`, whose construction is deferred until `_materialize_forcing(velocity_forcing, domain)` runs inside the body, after validation. That is precisely the fix the paragraph describes as not done. Since the author is finder, fixer and reporter of record, a reader trusting the commit message would conclude this defect is still open when the code already closed it — exactly the failure mode an independent audit exists to catch.

findings.title: ModelSpectrum's public contract was narrowed (arity 4→3, provenance now hard-fails on non-preset combinations) beyond what the stated GPU/bitstype defect required, and no claim discloses the narrowing
findings.before:
struct ModelSpectrum{L<:LargeScaleFactor, D<:DissipationFactor} <: EnergySpectrum
  C_K::Float64
  large_scale::L
  dissipation::D
  ref::Reference
end
...
provenance(m::ModelSpectrum) = m.ref
findings.after:
struct ModelSpectrum{L<:LargeScaleFactor, D<:DissipationFactor} <: EnergySpectrum
  C_K::Float64
  large_scale::L
  dissipation::D
end
...
provenance(m::ModelSpectrum) = _reference(m.large_scale, m.dissipation)
_reference(::PopeLargeScale, ::PopeDissipation) = _POPE2000
_reference(::VonKarmanLarge, ::UnitDissipation) = _VONKARMAN1948
_reference(::UnitLargeScale, ::PaoDissipation) = _PAO1965
_reference(::LargeScaleFactor, ::DissipationFactor) =
  throw(ArgumentError("this combination of large-scale and dissipation factors is not a published " *
                      "model, so it has no reference; the named presets each carry one"))
findings.why_it_matters: The claim (in the "Close out the third pass" commit) is scoped to a bitstype/GPU-launch defect: "a `Phenomenology`-seeded run could not start on a GPU at all (`ModelSpectrum` carried its bibliographic `Reference` as a FIELD, making it non-bitstype …)". That defect is fixed by simply not storing `ref` in the struct. But the edit goes further: it drops `ref` from the plain positional constructor entirely (4 args → 3, a breaking signature change for any positional caller) and hard-codes `provenance` to recognize only three named (large_scale, dissipation) pairs, throwing `ArgumentError` for anything else. The module's own docstring on this type invites building custom combinations directly ("Build one directly to mix roll-off forms, or use a preset"), consistent with the `Phenomenology` module's stated purpose as a strategy pattern for adding new author-year parametrizations. A user who previously built a `ModelSpectrum` with a bespoke (large_scale, dissipation) pairing and their own citation could do so before this change; after it, the same construction still succeeds but `provenance()` on it now throws, and no route to attach a custom reference for a non-preset combination exists at all. No round's commit message mentions this narrowing — every message describes only the bitstype removal.

findings.title: Docstring prose left referring to the removed `ref` parameter — the fix that removed it was applied incompletely to its own home
findings.before:
ModelSpectrum(C_K, large_scale, dissipation, ref)
...
an inertial-range core with Kolmogorov constant `C_K` times a large-scale roll-off `large_scale` (a
[`LargeScaleFactor`](@ref), giving ``f_L``) and a dissipation-range roll-off `dissipation` (a
[`DissipationFactor`](@ref), giving ``f_\eta``); `ref` is its [`Reference`](@ref). Build one directly to
mix roll-off forms, or use a preset such as [`Pope2000`](@ref).
...
The plain constructor `ModelSpectrum(C_K, large_scale, dissipation, ref)` takes the four fields
directly, in the order shown:
...
- `ref` — the `Reference` reported as the model's provenance.
findings.after:
ModelSpectrum(C_K, large_scale, dissipation)
...
an inertial-range core with Kolmogorov constant `C_K` times a large-scale roll-off `large_scale` (a
[`LargeScaleFactor`](@ref), giving ``f_L``) and a dissipation-range roll-off `dissipation` (a
[`DissipationFactor`](@ref), giving ``f_\eta``); `ref` is its [`Reference`](@ref). Build one directly to
mix roll-off forms, or use a preset such as [`Pope2000`](@ref).
...
The plain constructor `ModelSpectrum(C_K, large_scale, dissipation)` takes the three fields
directly, in the order shown:
- `C_K` — …
- `large_scale` — …
- `dissipation` — …
findings.why_it_matters: The signature line and the `# Fields` list were both updated to drop `ref` (4 args to 3), but the identity-sentence prose in between — "`ref` is its [`Reference`](@ref)" — was left untouched and now names a parameter/field that no longer exists anywhere in the type. A reader of the rendered docstring hits an internal contradiction within a few lines: the signature and Fields list say three arguments, the prose still asserts a fourth. This is a direct byproduct of the very edit whose commit message frames the change as a complete field removal, landed incompletely on the docstring that is its own home.

findings.title: CFL ceiling silently halves (or worse) the timestep of every run whose peak speed is below 1
findings.before: -  return speed > 0 ? sim.cfl * Δx / speed : sim.cfl * Δx
findings.after:
+  ceiling = sim.cfl * Δx
+  return speed > 0 ? min(sim.cfl * Δx / speed, ceiling) : ceiling
findings.why_it_matters: The stated defect is Δt diverging as u_max→0 in a decaying run. The clamp applied is not a limit at u_max→0: it binds at every u_max < 1, and "1" is a bare number compared against a dimensional velocity, so the ceiling depends on the units the box and energy are expressed in. Measured on a live run (16³, ν=0.05, unforced, kinetic_energy=0.02): max_speed=0.514, old rule Δt=0.3822, new Δt=0.1963 — a 1.95x cut at t=0, growing without bound as the run decays. Every unforced/decaying run, every low-amplitude run, and every run in units where u=O(0.1) now takes several times more steps; a script gated on step count (`current_step(s) < 200`) now covers a different span of simulated time, and any recorded time series changes. The same commit set writes the contradicting rule into a new error message two hundred lines up — "`cfl` must be positive ... it scales the advective timestep Δt = cfl·Δx/u_max" — and the function's own header comment still reads "Δt = C·Δx/maxᵢ|uᵢ|". A bound at u_max→0 needs a run-derived velocity scale or an explicit max_dt setting, not the value the rule happens to give at unit speed.
findings.disposition: CONFIRMED BY HAND — measured 1.9x cut (max_speed 0.525: 0.374 -> 0.196). The ceiling binds at u_max < 1, a bare number against a dimensional velocity, so it is unit-dependent. OPEN, for the user.

findings.title: The empty-band forcing guard was deleted, not rescaled: near-empty bands are now amplified by up to 10⁷ in one call
findings.before:
-  band_value < 1e-12 && return field                   # nothing in the band yet (guard)
-  amplitude = band_observable > 1e-12 ? forcing.injection_rate / (2 * band_observable) : 0.0
findings.after:
+_band_is_empty(band_value) = !(isfinite(band_value) && band_value > zero(band_value))
+  _band_is_empty(band_value) && return field           # nothing in the band yet
+  amplitude = _band_is_empty(band_observable) ? 0.0 :
+              forcing.injection_rate / (2 * band_observable)
findings.why_it_matters: The floor's job was numerical, not scale-setting: it stopped `scale = sqrt(target_band / band_value)` and `injection_rate / (2*band_observable)` from dividing by a band that carries only round-off. Positivity does not do that job. Measured: a valid velocity field with band observable 1.4e-14 previously took the skip branch; it now goes through one `apply_forcing!` that lifts k from 1.5e-14 to 1.4999999999999991 — an amplitude multiplier of ~10⁷ applied to what is numerically noise, in a single step. `ConstantPower` has the same exposure through its amplitude. The branch also flipped the other way for non-finite input: `NaN < 1e-12` was false, so a blown-up field used to propagate NaN through the forcing visibly; `_band_is_empty(NaN)` is true, so the forcing now silently no-ops on it. If the scale-invariance argument is the real one, the replacement should have been a relative floor against the field's own observable, not the removal of any floor.

findings.title: In-place `randn!` removes the host-generate-then-copy that made StochasticOU work on device backends
findings.before: -  copyto!(field_data(noise_physical), randn(ou.rng, T, size(field_data(noise_physical))...))
findings.after:
+  # In place: `randn` would allocate a fresh field-scale array on every step of the hot loop, and on
+  # a device backend a host array to copy across as well.
+  randn!(ou.rng, field_data(noise_physical))
findings.why_it_matters: The deleted line was not naive: it drew on the host and `copyto!`-ed across, which is the only way a `MersenneTwister` can fill a `CuArray`/`ROCArray`. `Random.randn!(::AbstractRNG, ::AbstractArray)` has no device method — the generic fallback assigns element by element, which a device array rejects as scalar indexing. So on this package's primary target the stochastic forcing goes from working to erroring at the first `prepare_forcing!`, and the comment records the transfer it removed as pure waste. The fix also inverts the invariant it cites: dropping one host allocation per step is bought with the loss of the GPU path entirely. If the allocation was the concern, the host buffer should have been hoisted onto the forcing beside `noise_physical`.
findings.disposition: DISPUTED, NOT DISMISSED — flagged independently by three lanes. An earlier round-5 witness ran on the RTX 5070 Ti under allowscalar(false) and passed, citing GPUArrays' own randn! method. Corroboration outweighs my single counter-witness; needs a real GPU check before anyone acts. OPEN.

findings.title: Moving the Lagrangian sample history into the cache makes `fields_modified!` silently demote AdamsBashforth to its bootstrap scheme
findings.after:
+  if cache.history_filled < K - 1            # no history yet: start up on the one-step scheme
+function allocate_buffers(::AdamsBashforth{K}, tracers::Tracers, cache) where {K}
+fields_modified!(cache::ObservablesCache) =
+  (advance_fields_epoch!(cache); cache.history_filled = 0; cache)
findings.why_it_matters: The history is now the cache's, and `fields_modified!` clears it. That verb is the documented announcement for any out-of-band state change — State.jl's own seeding note tells users to call it, and a hand-run `step!` loop that announces its field advance the documented way now zeroes the history on every iteration, pinning an `AdamsBashforth(order=4)` in its `EndpointHeun` bootstrap forever. The trajectory integration order silently drops with no error and no warning; only `cache.history_filled` would show it. Verified: after six `advance!` calls history_filled = 3, and one `fields_modified!(sim.cache)` takes it to 0. Separately, the exported two-argument `allocate_buffers(scheme, tracers)` no longer exists for a multistep scheme — verified MethodError — so the documented hand-assembly path ("the scheme's per-step storage is yours to allocate") is broken for AdamsBashforth, and `MultistepBuffers`'s public fields (`past`, `steps`, `filled`) are gone.

findings.title: The newly added `fields_modified!(sim)` convenience is a distinct, unimported generic and always throws
findings.before:
-using ..Cache: ObservablesCache, check_deposits, particles_modified!, deposit_sample!,
-               velocity_physical, max_speed, particle_velocities
findings.after:
+import ..Cache: particles_modified!
+using ..Cache: ObservablesCache, check_deposits, deposit_sample!, advance_particles_epoch!,
+               velocity_physical, max_speed, particle_velocities
+fields_modified!(sim::Simulation) = (fields_modified!(sim.cache); sim)
findings.why_it_matters: `particles_modified!` is imported so its `Simulation` method extends the cache generic; `fields_modified!` is not imported, so line 536 creates a second, unrelated `SimulationRun.fields_modified!` holding only the `::Simulation` method. Its body then calls itself with an `ObservablesCache` and dies. Verified: `IT.SimulationRun.fields_modified!(sim)` throws `MethodError: no method matching fields_modified!(::ObservablesCache{...})`, and `methods` shows two distinct generics. The public name `GBGHomogeneousTurbulence.fields_modified!` still resolves to the cache verb, so the run form is unreachable as well as broken. The change was added purely for symmetry with the particle form — its own comment says so — and ships untested and non-functional.

findings.title: `step!` changed its return value from the `(û, φ̂)` pair to `state`, breaking destructuring callers
findings.before:
-  fields_modified!(cache)                     # the step advanced the fields — the cache goes stale
-  return û, φ̂
findings.after:
+  advance_fields_epoch!(cache)                # the step advanced the fields — the cache goes stale
+  return state
findings.why_it_matters: Both scheme methods changed together, so every hand-run loop written against what `step!` actually returned — `û, φ̂ = step!(...)`, the natural spelling for the pair it handed back — now fails, since `ResolvedFields` is not iterable. The defect found was a docstring/code disagreement; the resolution picked the side that breaks working callers rather than the side that breaks nothing, on a package whose stated position is that the API is not frozen but which also has no deprecation path. Worth flagging as a deliberate contract change so it is not discovered by a user's loop.

findings.title: The `particle_velocities` staleness "fix" is a semantic no-op shipped with a comment asserting a defect that never existed
findings.before:
-  cache.sample_fields_epoch == cache.fields_epoch &&
-    cache.sample_particles_epoch == cache.particles_epoch ||
-    error("the cached particle velocities are stale: ...")
findings.after:
+  # BOTH epochs, because the sample is a function of the state AND the positions ... Testing only the
+  # fields epoch left the announced reposition ... invisible to the read ...
+  (cache.sample_fields_epoch == cache.fields_epoch &&
+   cache.sample_particles_epoch == cache.particles_epoch) ||
+    error("the cached particle velocities are stale: ...")
findings.why_it_matters: `&&` binds tighter than `||` in Julia, so `a && b || error(...)` already parsed as `(a && b) || error(...)` — confirmed by evaluation and by reading the file at 569e6fc, where both epoch tests were present. The parentheses change nothing. What was added is a six-line comment stating, as recorded history, that the old read tested only the fields epoch, that a sample along an abandoned trajectory "was served as current", and that "`advance!`'s opening guard could never fire" — none of which was ever true. The code is harmless; the comment now misinforms every future reader about the cache's failure history, and this is the one edit in the round that fixed nothing at all, which matters for how much weight the round's other claims carry.

findings.title: A per-step scalar reduction and device readback was added to `advance!`, outside the frozen synchronization ledger, and its throw leaves the clock behind the state
findings.before:
-  check_deposits(sim.cache)
-
-  sim.clock.time += Δt
-  sim.clock.step += 1
findings.after:
+  isfinite(max_speed(sim.cache)) ||
+    error("non-finite velocity at step $(sim.clock.step + 1): the run appears to have blown up")
+  sim.state.scalar_spectral === nothing ||
+    isfinite(scalar_variance(sim.state.scalar_spectral)) ||
+    error("non-finite scalar at step $(sim.clock.step + 1): the run appears to have blown up")
findings.why_it_matters: For every scalar-carrying run this adds one full quadratic spectral reduction plus one blocking device-to-host readback to every iteration, unconditionally — the hot loop the footprint/compute invariant governs. test/optimality_audit.jl transcribes the per-step synchronization sites by hand (`deposit!`, `StationarityCriterion`, `_observe_and_test!`, the forcings) and freezes achieved-vs-floor counts; it lists `Sync("scalar variance", ...)` only under `monitor === :skew_scalar`. That file is untouched in this range (only test/memory_audit.jl moved), so the new site is unledgered and unheld — the exact "unclaimed gap" the audit exists to fail on, invisible because the ledger is a transcription. Behaviourally, a run that goes non-finite now raises out of `advance!` after the state has been advanced and deposited but before `sim.clock` is updated, so a caller that catches the error holds a run whose fields are one step ahead of its clock and step counter; previously the iteration completed and the NaNs were visible in the next diagnostic.

findings.title: The new CFL ceiling silently caps the adaptive timestep for any sub-unit-speed run, not just the resting one the fix was aimed at
findings.before: return speed > 0 ? sim.cfl * Δx / speed : sim.cfl * Δx
findings.after:
ceiling = sim.cfl * Δx
  return speed > 0 ? min(sim.cfl * Δx / speed, ceiling) : ceiling
findings.why_it_matters: The documented rule is Δt = cfl·Δx/u_max (restated verbatim in the new `advance!` validation message: "it scales the advective timestep Δt = cfl·Δx/u_max"). The genuine defect was the exact-speed-zero fallback (measured Δt≈1e15). But the fix does not bound only that limit — it caps Δt at `sim.cfl * Δx` for EVERY step where `max_speed(cache) < 1`, treating 'unit speed' as a universal reference even though the package normalizes nothing to guarantee that. For the fully-documented, first-class use case of freely decaying turbulence (`NoForcing()`, explicitly named in `StationarityCriterion`'s and the architecture's own docs), u_max decreases continuously as the flow decays; every such run, once max speed drops below 1 (in whatever units `kinetic_energy`/`side_length` were given), now takes a smaller step than the advective-CFL rule would allow, silently changing the number of steps needed to reach a given simulated time and the times at which observables are recorded — for input that was previously valid and produced a different, larger, still-correct Δt. The regression test added for this fix (`test/regressions/03-numerics-and-types-03-cfl-zero-speed.jl`) only exercises `max_speed == 0` exactly; the continuously-capped regime (0 < speed < 1) is untested and its docstring (`advance!`: "the step size is the advective-CFL value for the current velocity") was not updated to mention the cap.
findings.disposition: CONFIRMED BY HAND — measured 1.9x cut (max_speed 0.525: 0.374 -> 0.196). The ceiling binds at u_max < 1, a bare number against a dimensional velocity, so it is unit-dependent. OPEN, for the user.

findings.title: The band-emptiness test dropped its floor entirely, reopening the division-by-~0 hazard its own surviving docstrings say is guarded against
findings.before: band_value < 1e-12 && return field                   # nothing in the band yet (guard)
findings.after:
_band_is_empty(band_value) && return field           # nothing in the band yet

_band_is_empty(band_value) = !(isfinite(band_value) && band_value > zero(band_value))
findings.why_it_matters: The stated defect is real (an absolute 1e-12 floor breaks the scalar equation's φ→sφ scale invariance for a genuinely small-amplitude or Float32 run). But the replacement doesn't narrow the floor to a scale-appropriate one — it removes it outright, testing exact positivity instead. `apply_forcing!` then computes `scale = sqrt(target_band / band_value)`, and `set_forcing_rate!`'s `ConstantPower` twin computes `forcing.injection_rate / (2 * band_observable)` — both diverge for a `band_value`/`band_observable` that is a tiny positive floating-point residue rather than exactly 0 or negative, which is exactly the 'empty band' case a band-pass kernel with round-off at its shell edges can produce. The two docstrings this same change touches were left unedited and now contradict the code: `BandRescaling`'s says '**below a small floor** the rescale returns the field untouched rather than dividing by ~0' (Forcing.jl, BandRescaling docstring) and `ConstantPower`'s says 'Below a small floor on E_band the rate is set to zero instead, so an empty band stays empty rather than receiving an unbounded kick' (Forcing.jl, ConstantPower docstring) — both describe a floor that no longer exists, and a run whose band content is at floating-point noise level (previously silently treated as empty and skipped, exactly as documented) can now receive an enormous spurious rescale/amplitude instead.

findings.title: StationarityCriterion's non-positive-dissipation branch now bypasses both the stationarity test and the max_turnovers give-up path it used to reach
findings.before: ε > 0 && (criterion.elapsed_turn += Δt * ε / Float64(kinetic_energy(sim.state.velocity_spectral)))
findings.after:
if ε > 0
    criterion.elapsed_turn += Δt * ε / Float64(kinetic_energy(sim.state.velocity_spectral))
  else
    @warn "StationarityCriterion: the dissipation rate is not positive (ε = $ε), so the eddy-turnover ... clock cannot advance and stationarity can never be detected — stopping. ..."
    return false
  end
  _observe_and_test!(criterion.monitor, sim, criterion.elapsed_turn, ε) && return false
findings.why_it_matters: Previously, a single sample with ε ≤ 0 only skipped the turnover-clock increment for that iteration; the callback still ran `_observe_and_test!` (which could still detect stationarity from already-accumulated `elapsed_turn`) and still checked `elapsed_turn ≥ max_turnovers` on subsequent iterations, so a transient non-positive ε could not derail an otherwise-converging or already-capped run. The new code returns `false` (stop the run, per `run!`'s contract) on the very first such sample, unconditionally, skipping both of those checks for that call. The fix correctly closes the infinite-loop failure mode for a genuinely non-dissipating run, but it also changes behavior for any run where ε dips to exactly 0 only transiently (e.g. numerical underflow at a sample instant) — such a run previously could still reach and report its `max_turnovers` cap or detect stationarity; it now stops immediately with a different warning and never gets the chance.
